summary: The main article describes a palladium(II)/chiral phosphoric acid catalyzed three-component reaction involving bond cleavage and reassembly. It includes 5 figures and 2 tables in the main text detailing the conceptual framework, optimization, and mechanistic studies.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Conceptual framework. ( a ) Intramolecular rearrangement: bond cleavage and reconstruction. ( b ) Concept of bond cleavage, fragment modification and reassembly.
items.description: This figure illustrates the theoretical difference between traditional intramolecular rearrangements and the proposed multi-component bond cleavage/reassembly process.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Discovery of the novel process. ( a ) Prior works for the enantioselective trapping of zwitterionic intermediates. ( b ) Hypothetical pathway for the enamine-participated multi-component reaction. ( c ) Actual process: bond cleavage, fragment modification and reassembly.
items.description: This figure contrasts previous work on zwitterionic trapping with the newly discovered three-component reaction involving C-N bond cleavage.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Optimization for the enantioselective three-component reaction of 2 and 3a with 4a*.
items.description: This table details the screening of various chiral phosphoric acids, solvents, and temperatures to optimize the yield and enantioselectivity of the reaction.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Discussion on the reaction pathway. ( a ) Control reaction to exclude the formation of 5c from aziridine 7 . ( b ) Proposed reaction pathway for the formation of 6 via iminium intermediate C . ( c ) Control reaction to exclude the formation of 5c from N-H insertion product 9 . ( d ) Reaction under the catalysis of a premade palladium/phosphate complex to confirm the active catalyst.
items.description: This figure presents several control experiments and proposed pathways to elucidate the mechanism and identify the active catalytic species.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Putative reaction pathways. Cycle I: formation of iminium salt C; cycle II: formation of ammonium ylides.
items.description: A detailed catalytic cycle showing the formation of iminium salts and ammonium ylides leading to the final product.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.caption: The additional evidence and structure determination. ( a ) Cross-coupling control experiment reaction to confirm the C-N bond cleavage. ( b ) Reduction of enamine intermediate G to diamines 11a and 11b , and the structure determination of 11b by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis.
items.description: This figure provides experimental evidence for the C-N bond cleavage and the absolute configuration of the products via X-ray analysis.

items.heading: 5c
items.caption: (2R,3S)-adamantan-1-yl 3-(4-bromophenyl)-5-oxo-2,5-diphenyl-2-(phenylamino)pentanoate
items.description: Characterization data for product 5c, including NMR and HRMS data.

items.heading: 11a
items.caption: (2R,3S,5R)-adamantan-1-yl 3-(4-bromophenyl)-5-morpholino-2,5-diphenyl-2(phenylamino)pentanoate
items.description: Characterization data for the reduced diamine product 11a.

items.heading: 11b
items.caption: (2R,3S,5S)-adamantan-1-yl 3-(4-bromophenyl)-5-morpholino-2,5-diphenyl-2-(phenylamino)pentanoate
items.description: Characterization data for the reduced diamine product 11b, whose structure was confirmed by X-ray.
